recovery_proof.inline_source_extraction: Independently decoded all18 original JSON cmd literals and quoted Python heredoc bodies; exact archived bytes, call raw-line hashes and output-event hashes match. AST parsed only; no source executed.
recovery_proof.record08_v1: Exact creation/static-derivation/output/v2-launch events distinguish retained unexecuted v1 from executed v2.

limits: Historical .py.txt archives are source data; do not execute or reformat them. Current scripts/batch079*.py are separate linted copies.

Three early sources are literal creation-payload extractions. No contemporaneous original runtime digest was retained; exact successor comparisons and original receipts provide separate supporting evidence.
Two intermediate runner states are deterministic Ruff/Black reconstructions, not directly captured old runtime files.
Full session logs and ignored source/command artifacts are not published. Only exact helper sources and task-specific evidence metadata are included.
The pre-Path.home runner retains a historical workstation PATH literal as exact non-executable source data.

The archive inventories the known retained helper versions, recovered executed early states, two record10 inline amendments and eighteen task-scoped chemical audit heredocs. Read-only shell browsing, unrelated session context and packaging/recovery commands are not a general command-transcript archive. Some historical outputs omitted an explicit process exit code; those entries retain null and their actual completion events.
argv_convention: argv_display is display-normalized metadata: $CHECKOUT replaces the historical absolute checkout path and $UV replaces the historical absolute uv executable. The separately hash-pinned original receipt is authoritative for exact raw argv; no normalized display is claimed to be the original command string.
